To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

chronic lymphocytic leukaemia cells metabolize free fatty acids (FAFAs), that lipoprotein lipases are responsible for this, and that STAT3 is responsible for the aberrant lipoprotein lipse expression.

1) CLL cells metabolize free fatty acids (FAs); 2) STAT3 is constituitively activated in CLL and drives the aberrant LPL expression in CLL cells; 3) inhibition of LPL reduces the capacity of CLL to metabolize FAs and decreases CLL cell viability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the metabolism of CLL cells, which we found to be distinct from that of normal B cells.
understanding the molecular and cellular basis of the metabolic changes that occur in CLL cells.
the role of STAT3 in the pathogenesis of CLL.

LPL is a novel therapeutic target in CLL.

we have shown that CLL cells metabolize Fatty Acids (FAs) and that the activation of STAT3 drives LPL expression, which catalyzers the hydrolysis triglycerides to FAs, and therefore, STAT3 inhibition may be a therapeutic option to prevent CLL cell metabolism.
